h1: The 6 Best Mandoline Slicers With Hand Guards and Safer Blades, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mandolines With Hand Guards: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 mandoline slicers scored on food holders, hidden blades, thickness range, stability, storage and blade safety locks.
summary: The OXO Good Grips Precision handheld is the mandoline to buy if safety is the point, because an automatic, height-adjustable food holder keeps fingers away from the blade and the holder stores on the board. The SupMaKin and ONCE FOR ALL hide the blade entirely, the Ibergrif adds a storage lock, and the Gramercy is for precise slicing.
intro: Most mandoline injuries do not happen during the cut. They happen at the end of it, when the last third of a vegetable is too small to hold and you push it through anyway. A hand guard only protects you if it holds the food all the way down, and if you actually use it.

So this ranking looks at how each mandoline keeps hands away from the blade, from food holders and hidden blades to storage locks. We reviewed six models from their listings, comparing guard design, thickness range, cut options, stability and blade material. Several listings do not name a guard, and we flag those instead of assuming one is included.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Precision Handheld Mandoline
products.verdict: An automatic, height-adjustable food holder, five cut options and a slim handheld body.
products.description:
The OXO Precision is a slim handheld mandoline with five cutting options, including julienne and thin, and an automatic, height-adjustable food holder that stores on the board.

It ranks first because the holder is the guard, and it adapts to the height of the food, so it keeps gripping as the vegetable shrinks. That addresses the real danger point at the end of a cut. Because the holder stores on the board, it is always there when you need it, which is not true of loose guards. It has fewer thickness steps than the Gramercy's twelve.

Buy it if you want the holder to do most of the guarding. A slim handheld body is less stable than a large base model.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want the holder to do most of the guarding.
products.skipIf: You want twelve precise thickness settings.

products.name: SupMaKin Safer Mandoline Slicer 1-8 mm
products.verdict: Built-in stainless blades you never touch, a 0.1 to 8 mm range and a push handle.
products.description:
The SupMaKin has built-in, heavy-duty stainless steel blades, a 0.1 to 8 mm thickness range and a push-handle slicing action.

It ranks second because it removes the hazard instead of guarding it: with the blade built in, there is nothing to touch in normal use. The 0.1 to 8 mm range covers paper-thin potato chips to thick cuts, and a push handle takes your fingers out of the path. It sits behind the OXO because the listing does not describe stability features or a food holder.

Choose it for a blade you never have to touch. Check the listing for cleaning instructions, since an enclosed blade can trap food.
pros: Blade is built in, never touched
products.idealFor: Cooks who prefer a blade they never have to touch.
products.skipIf: You want a food holder you can see working.

products.name: ONCE FOR ALL Upgrade Safe Mandoline Slicer Plus
products.verdict: A hidden blade, a larger feeding port, four modes and a collapsible body.
products.description:
The ONCE FOR ALL slicer has a hidden sharp blade, a larger feeding port, four mode choices and a collapsible design.

It ranks third because the larger feeding port takes whole onions and bigger potatoes without pre-cutting, which saves time on large batches, and the hidden blade matches the SupMaKin's protection. It slips behind that model because the listing gives no thickness range and says nothing about how stable the base is once the hinge is open.

Buy it for larger batches where hiding the blade matters most, and where you want compact storage. A collapsible build can wobble if the hinge loosens.
products.idealFor: Batch cooks who slice many vegetables and want the blade hidden.
products.skipIf: You want a stated thickness range.

products.name: Ibergrif Handheld Mandoline Slicer
products.verdict: Three thicknesses, an included food holder, a blade safety lock and a non-slip design.
products.description:
The Ibergrif has three adjustable thicknesses, an included food holder, a blade safety lock, a non-slip design and a stainless steel blade.

It ranks fourth because the blade lock covers the other time a mandoline injures you: when you reach into a drawer or wash it. A food holder is included, which is the baseline guard, and a non-slip design helps stability. It has fewer thickness settings than the OXO Precision and no automatic height adjustment on the holder.

Choose it for occasional cooking where a lock gives safe storage. Remember that a manual holder only helps if you use it every time.
products.idealFor: Occasional cooks who want a lock for safe storage.
products.skipIf: You want a holder that adjusts automatically.

products.name: Gramercy Mandoline Slicer 12 Settings
products.verdict: Twelve slice settings on a built-in dial, a 4CR15 stainless blade and anti-slip feet.
products.description:
The Gramercy has 12 slice settings on a built-in thickness dial, a 4CR15 stainless steel blade and a non-slip base with anti-slip feet.

It ranks fifth because its strength is precision and stability, not guarding. A dial with 12 steps lets you choose an exact thickness, and anti-slip feet keep a base-style slicer from sliding on a wet counter. The listing does not mention a food holder or hand guard, so you must supply your own protection.

Pick it if you slice often and value precision and a steady base. Use cut-resistant gloves, since no guard is listed.
pros: Anti-slip feet on a stable base
products.idealFor: Frequent slicers who value precision and a steady base.
products.skipIf: You want a guard included in the listing.

products.name: OXO Good Grips Handheld Mandoline Slicer
products.verdict: Three thickness settings, a large non-slip handle and a stable foot that hooks over a bowl.
products.description:
The OXO Good Grips handheld mandoline slices at 1, 2.5 and 4 mm, with a large non-slip handle, a stable foot and a hook that rests over a bowl.

It ranks last because the listing describes a foot and bowl hook but no hand guard or food holder, which is the feature this guide values most. The roomy non-slip handle is a genuine control advantage, and slicing straight into a bowl is tidy, but three fixed settings trail the OXO Precision's five cutting options.

Buy it if you want a stable, simple slicer with a comfortable handle. Add a separate guard or cut-resistant glove, since the product alone does not shield your fingers.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a simple slicer with a roomy handle.
products.skipIf: A built-in food holder is a must.

methodology.title: Hand protection
methodology.description: Food holders, hidden blades and safety locks carried the most weight, since protection is the point of this ranking.

methodology.title: Thickness range
methodology.description: Stated settings, from three steps to 0.1 to 8 mm, show how many cuts a mandoline can handle.

methodology.title: Stability
methodology.description: Non-slip feet, bowl hooks and wide handles keep the slicer steady while you push.

methodology.title: Blade quality
methodology.description: Stainless steel and named alloys such as 4CR15 were noted, though blade sharpness over time is not listed.

methodology.title: Storage
methodology.description: Collapsible bodies, holders that store on board and blade locks reduce risk when the slicer is put away.

whatMatters.detail: A food holder grips the vegetable so your fingers never enter the blade path, and it matters most for the last third of a cut, where most injuries happen. The OXO Precision's holder is automatic and height adjustable, so it keeps gripping as the food shortens. Look for a named holder in the listing, and confirm it stores with the tool.

A hidden or enclosed blade removes the exposed edge during normal slicing, which is the SupMaKin's and the ONCE FOR ALL's main safety claim. The tradeoff is cleaning, because food can lodge inside the assembly. Look for the words built in or hidden, and check how the blade section comes apart for washing before you buy.

A blade lock or cover protects you in storage and while washing, which is when many mandoline cuts actually happen, since people reach into a drawer or rinse the blade blindly. The Ibergrif lists a blade lock; most others do not. Look for a lock or cover in the listing, and if absent, plan to store it in a case.

Thickness range defines which dishes the mandoline can handle. The SupMaKin spans 0.1 to 8 mm, the Gramercy offers 12 settings on a dial, and the OXO Good Grips has fixed 1, 2.5 and 4 mm steps. Wider range means finer control but more setting to verify. Check the stated range and match it to how you cook.

Stability controls how hard you push, and pushing hard is how hands slip. The Gramercy has anti-slip feet, the OXO Good Grips a stable foot and bowl hook, and the Ibergrif a non-slip design. A slicer that creeps on a wet counter is a hazard. Look for named anti-slip features, and put a damp cloth under any base without them.

faq.q: Do I still need a cut-resistant glove?
faq.a: It is a sensible extra. Even with the OXO Precision's holder, the last piece of a vegetable is hard to grip, and models like the Gramercy list no guard at all. A glove adds a layer for the few seconds that matter.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Not using the guard. A holder only protects when it is on every slice, and the end of the vegetable is when people take it off. Stop slicing when the piece gets small, and cut the rest by knife.

faq.q: Is a mandoline worth it over a knife?
faq.a: For uniform slices and speed, yes. A SupMaKin's 0.1 to 8 mm range gives consistency that a knife struggles with. For occasional cooks, a sharp knife is safer than a mandoline with no guard.

faq.q: How do I set the thickness?
faq.a: Choose the setting before you start, check it with a test slice and lock it in place. The Gramercy's dial has 12 steps, while the Ibergrif has three. Do not adjust with food on the blade.

faq.q: How do I clean a mandoline safely?
faq.a: Use a brush under running water, always moving away from the edge, and never wipe the blade with a cloth. A hidden blade like the ONCE FOR ALL's needs the collapsing parts washed separately.

faq.q: Can I slice soft foods like tomatoes?
faq.a: It depends on blade sharpness and the thickness setting. A thicker slice from the OXO Good Grips at 4 mm helps. Very ripe tomatoes may squash, so choose a firm one and a sharp blade.

finalTake: The OXO Precision is the safest everyday choice because its holder adjusts to the food and stays on the board. Choose the SupMaKin or ONCE FOR ALL if you want the blade out of reach, and the Ibergrif if storage safety matters. The Gramercy and the plain OXO are precise or comfortable, but they list no guard.
